cf.title: Track skipped vacuum and analyze in pg_stat_all_tables

input.subject: Track skipped tables during autovacuum and autoanalyze

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread, and no surviving objection is fatal. The decisive point is security-1: message #51 shows that a role without privileges on a table can bump its skip counters, and v20 does not fix it. The other surviving points (already-exists-1, maintenance-fit-1, maintenance-fit-2) are fixable scope and layout questions that a committer who knows the cumulative statistics code can settle.

brief.title: Track lock-skipped vacuum and analyze in pg_stat_all_tables
brief.problem: When autovacuum, autoanalyze or a manual VACUUM/ANALYZE with SKIP_LOCKED skips a table because the lock is not available, Postgres only writes a log message. Users who monitor tables that have not been vacuumed for a long time cannot see per table whether autovacuum is trying and being skipped, or not running at all.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds eight per-relation statistics fields: a last-skip timestamp and a skip counter for each of manual vacuum, autovacuum, manual analyze and autoanalyze. They are exposed in pg_stat_all_tables. The skip is reported when the conditional lock fails. A second syscache lookup drops a stats entry created for a concurrently dropped relation, and relkinds that the view cannot display are filtered out.
user_visible_surface: New pg_stat_all_tables columns last_lock_skipped_vacuum, last_lock_skipped_autovacuum, last_lock_skipped_analyze, last_lock_skipped_autoanalyze.
New pg_stat_all_tables columns lock_skipped_vacuum_count, lock_skipped_autovacuum_count, lock_skipped_analyze_count, lock_skipped_autoanalyze_count.
Eight new pg_stat_get_* functions, for example pg_stat_get_last_lock_skipped_vacuum_time.
A changed stats file format that needs a PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID bump, left for the committer.
A documentation note that a skipped manual command on a parent table is recorded only on the parent, not on its children.
author_claims: The timestamps show that autovacuum is attempting to run and that the lack of progress comes from repeated skips.
The counters help dashboards spot spikes in skipped autovacuum and autoanalyze.
The fields count lock skips only, so a future skip reason would get its own counter.
All review comments up to v19 are addressed, and the author asks for Ready for Committer status.
brief.thread_state: Sami Imseih co-develops the patch, and Shinya Kato and Zsolt Parragi reviewed it through v20. Michael Paquier backs the timestamps. vignesh C then reported that any role that can see the schema can bump a table's skip counters without privileges, and no one has answered.
unclear: The material does not say how the privilege problem will be fixed, or whether the fix belongs in this patch or the proposed follow-up.
The patch does not say what eight more fields cost in shared memory for each relation stats entry.
The patch does not say whether the stats views should be split or a separate index stats kind added, as Sami and Michael suggested.
Foreign tables can be skipped by analyze, but the view does not show them, and the material gives no plan for them.

prior_attempts.title: More stats about skipped/executed vacuums
prior_attempts.reason: The visible messages do not show why. Only the author's repost of the patch is shown, with no review or reply.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 added many vacuum outcome columns, including a successive-failure count, and took a lock on each table inside the view. This proposal counts only lock skips and computes nothing at view time.

prior_attempts.title: Add parallel columns for seq scan and index scan on pg_stat_all_tables and _indexes
prior_attempts.quote: I think the question to which we don't have a clear answer is: for what purpose would you want to be able to distinguish parallel and non-parallel scans on a per-table basis?
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers doubted that per-table and per-index counts of parallel scans help with tuning, since parallel plans with Gather nodes are usually analyzed per statement. Michael Paquier added that the metrics committed in e7a9496de906 and 5d4298e75f25 may already cover the need. Robert Haas found no clear use case for these counters. The author agreed that the committed metrics were good enough for now.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 added per-table counters without a clear per-table use. This proposal states its use: telling a table that autovacuum keeps skipping from one it never tries.

objections.title: Roles without privileges on a table can bump its lock-skip statistics
objections.failure_scenario: A role with only USAGE on the schema runs `vacuum (skip_locked) t` in a loop while the owner's batch job holds a lock. The lock_skipped_vacuum_count of t grows and last_lock_skipped_vacuum moves forward. A DBA alerting on these columns sees false spikes or loses the real signal, and cannot tell who caused them.
objections.argument: Message #51 shows the skip is recorded before vacuum_is_permitted_for_relation(), and includes a test that reproduces it. Message #42 reported the same gap and suggested the RangeVarGetRelidExtended() callback. Message #43 left it for a later cleanup that "someone" may take on, and v20 still has the gap with no reply to #51. Today a role without privileges on t can affect only its own WARNING output. With this patch it writes to shared per-table statistics that other roles read and alert on.
objections.author_must_show: Will v21 check vacuum and analyze privileges before recording a skip, and does that check change the existing WARNING for roles without privileges?

critic.reasoning: Message #51 reproduces the gap on v20 with a test, and no one has answered it. Message #43 left the fix from message #42 as an optional follow-up, so the current patch does not handle it.

objections.title: Every index and table stats entry pays for eight vacuum-only fields
objections.failure_scenario: A site with hundreds of thousands of relations upgrades. Each PgStat_StatTabEntry in shared memory grows by eight 8-byte fields, for indexes too, though an index never records a lock skip. The site pays this memory whether or not anyone reads the new columns.
objections.argument: Message #7 notes that PgStat_StatTabEntry is shared by indexes and tables, and that the vacuum and analyze fields apply only to tables. Michael proposes a separate index stats kind as a start (messages #7, #9), but v20 does not do that split and does not state the added size. Earlier entries proposing that split were returned ([P12], [P14]), with no reason recorded, so the split is not assured to land first. The cost falls on all relations, but the gain goes only to tables under lock contention.
objections.author_must_show: How much does each relation stats entry grow, and should the index and table stats split land before this patch adds eight table-only fields?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 confirms that indexes share PgStat_StatTabEntry, so each index entry also grows by eight fields. The thread does not state the added size or decide on the split; P12 and P14 record no reason and add no support.

objections.title: Each future skip reason adds four or eight more view columns
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch tracks autovacuum skips caused by another worker, as raised in message #29. Under the rule in message #30 it adds its own counters and timestamps. pg_stat_all_tables then holds sixteen or more skip columns, and dashboards that use select * change on each release.
objections.argument: The lock_skipped_ naming was chosen because more skip reasons are expected (messages #29, #30, #33). It fixes the pattern of four modes times two fields per reason in the main table view. Sami asked in message #6 whether vacuum columns should move to a dedicated view, and the thread does not answer. With ten patches like this one, the view would no longer be usable.
objections.author_must_show: Should skip tracking go into a dedicated vacuum view or a single keyed form, so that a second skip reason does not add eight more columns to pg_stat_all_tables?

critic.reasoning: Message #30 says another skip reason would need its own counter, and message #6's question about a dedicated vacuum view has no answer. Sami does not expect a second reason, so the risk is moderate, but the layout question stays open.

objections.title: Manual SKIP_LOCKED counters repeat a warning the caller already gets
objections.failure_scenario: A maintenance script runs VACUUM (SKIP_LOCKED) and already receives "skipping vacuum of ... lock not available" as a WARNING. The four manual columns add only a second copy of that warning. They are also the path by which a role with no rights on a table can change its statistics, as message #51 shows.
objections.argument: Manual VACUUM and ANALYZE with SKIP_LOCKED already return a WARNING to the session that asked for the skip. The author first judged that warning sufficient (message #3) and added the manual columns at a reviewer's request (message #2). The motivating problem, autovacuum that tries and gets skipped, concerns only the autovacuum columns. The privilege report in message #51 has no answer yet, and it exists only on the manual path.
objections.author_must_show: Which users need manual skips in a shared view when their script already receives the WARNING, and is that worth the unprivileged-write path from message #51?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 concedes the WARNING already reports manual skips, and the thread shows one reviewer request and no user report for the manual columns. A per-table view is more convenient than the WARNING, but the thread does not show that need is common.

refuted.title: Eight columns land in pg_stat_all_tables while a stats split is still open
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool adds queries for the eight new pg_stat_all_tables columns in release 20. A later release moves vacuum and analyze columns into a dedicated view or a table-only stats kind. The tool's queries break on upgrade, and users have to migrate twice for one feature.
refuted.argument: Message #6 asks whether vacuum columns should move into a dedicated view, and message #7 argues for splitting index and table stats first. The thread never decides this, and the patch adds eight columns to the existing view anyway. Once a view column ships, it is hard to remove, so the placement decision cannot be deferred to a follow-up.
refuted.author_must_show: If vacuum activity later moves to its own view, are these eight columns part of that move, and why should they go into pg_stat_all_tables first?

critic.reasoning: The patch puts the columns next to last_autovacuum and autovacuum_count, which is existing practice. A later move of vacuum columns would break queries on all of them equally, and no such move is proposed in the thread.

refuted.title: Counter meaning would change when the privilege check is added
refuted.failure_scenario: A role with no privileges on table t runs VACUUM (SKIP_LOCKED) t in a loop while t is locked. This inflates lock_skipped_vacuum_count and moves last_lock_skipped_vacuum. A DBA reading the view sees contention that no legitimate job caused. Fixing this after release silently changes what the counter counts.
refuted.argument: Message #51 shows that the skip is recorded before vacuum_is_permitted_for_relation(), and no one answered that message. Message #42 suggested moving the check into the RangeVarGetRelidExtended() callback, and message #43 left that as an optional follow-up. If the order changes after release, the documented contract changes between minor or major versions. Monitoring alert baselines would then shift for no visible reason.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the privilege check run before the skip is recorded in this patch, so that the counters only ever count commands the role was allowed to run?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1. The changed counter meaning only arises if the privilege gap ships, and security-1 covers that gap.

refuted.title: Manual-command skip columns add per-relation cost with little shown demand
refuted.failure_scenario: A cluster with tens of thousands of tables and indexes pays for eight more 64-bit fields in every shared relation stats entry, indexes included. Only scripts that run VACUUM or ANALYZE with SKIP_LOCKED ever move the four manual columns. Those scripts already get a WARNING for each skip.
refuted.argument: The demand in the thread is for the autovacuum side: message #1 is about autovacuum, and message #3 concedes that manual skips already emit a WARNING. The manual columns came from one reviewer suggestion in message #2, with no user report behind them. PgStat_StatTabEntry is shared by tables and indexes (message #7), so the cost falls on every relation, and the split that would avoid it is not done ([P12], [P14] were returned). Message #51 shows the manual path also lets an unprivileged role write these counters.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users run SKIP_LOCKED maintenance scripts that cannot read the WARNING, and does that need justify four columns on every relation stats entry?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1 for the manual-column demand, and of maintenance-fit-1 for the per-entry cost.

touch_points.reason: The stats file format changes and needs a PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID bump.

touch_points.reason: Eight new pg_proc functions and eight new pg_stat_all_tables columns need a catversion bump.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds eight fields to the relation stats entry declared in pgstat.h.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Message #51 shows the skip is recorded before the vacuum privilege check.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Eight view columns and eight functions stay for good, and each new skip reason would add more.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Every relation stats entry in shared memory, indexes included, grows by eight fields.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the next version check vacuum and analyze privileges before recording a skip, and does that change the existing WARNING for roles without privileges?
Which users need manual SKIP_LOCKED skips in a shared view when their session already receives the WARNING?
How much does each relation stats entry grow, and should the index and table stats split land before this patch?
Should skip tracking go into a dedicated vacuum view, so that a second skip reason does not add eight more columns to pg_stat_all_tables?
Should a lock-skipped analyze of a foreign table be recorded anywhere, given that pg_stat_all_tables does not show foreign tables?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier took part in the thread on the stats layout and backs the timestamps. The owner needs to know the cumulative statistics code and the lock and privilege order in vacuum.c.
committability.liability: Eight view columns and eight functions that cannot be removed later, a larger relation stats entry for every table and index, and the handling of a concurrent drop in pgstat_relation.c.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted twenty versions and answered each review round through message #50. Message #51 has no reply yet.

priority.reason: Users who monitor autovacuum under lock contention gain a per-table signal that only the server log gives today. The patch is about 46 KiB at v20 with three reviewers, but the privilege gap from message #51 must be closed before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check the order of the lock attempt, the privilege check and the stats report in vacuum.c. It also could not check the syscache lookup that guards against a concurrent drop, or the real size of the stats entry.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: autovacuum may skip tables when session_authorization/role is set on database
precedents_retrieved.summary: Autovacuum workers skip tables when `alter database ... set session_authorization` names a non-superuser who does not own the tables. The patch sets the session user of each autovacuum worker to the bootstrap superuser when the worker starts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether this setting has any real use case. He said many other settings can break autovacuum, and that a fix should also cover other background processes. The author gave no use case. The commitfest manager returned the patch for lack of interest and asked for a stronger use case.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm rather unimpressed by this proposal, first because there are
probably ten other ways to break autovac with ill-considered settings,
and second because if we do want to consider this a supported case,
what about other background processes?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: autovacuum: add possibility to change priority of vacuumed tables
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Masahiko Sawada, Tomas Vondra, Andres Freund
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a table-level autovacuum setting, autovacuum_table_priority, that each autovacuum worker uses to sort its list of tables before vacuuming. The aim is to let users choose which tables autovacuum processes first.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Each worker sorts its own table list once at start, so a high-priority table still waits behind the rest of that list and gets no timely cleanup, and users would find the setting hard to understand. Tomas Vondra added that refreshing the list more often could starve low-priority tables, and that lowering vacuum_scale_factor or adding worker capacity addresses the real problem. Andres Freund judged the entry still in its design phase, and the author agreed it needs more thinking.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This proposed patch does not really improve that, as the tables are
sorted by priority only once at the beginning (in each worker). As
explained by Masahiko-san in one of the previous e-mails, it means the
patch does not guarantee timely cleanup of the high-priority tables.

precedents_retrieved.title: More stats about skipped/executed vacuums
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds columns to pg_stat_all_tables that report vacuum outcomes: whether the next autovacuum will run and of which kind, pages truncated or left untruncated, index scans, oldest xmin, the status of the last vacuum, and a count of successive autovacuum failures. Vacuum records cancellations and errors through pgstat_report_vacuum(), and the view takes an access share lock on each table to compute the vacuum requirement status.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the author's repost of the patch is shown, with no review or reply.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last_vacuum_index_scans in pg_stat_all_tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a last_vacuum_index_scans column to pg_stat_all_tables that shows how many index scans the last vacuum of each table needed. The author meant it as a signal for raising maintenance_work_mem or autovacuum_work_mem.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera objected that the column keeps only the last vacuum's value, unlike other stats counters, which are all additive; he and Peter Geoghegan said a history of vacuum runs would be more useful. Fujii Masao asked whether one global counter in a pg_stat_vacuum view would be enough, and Alvaro later doubted the tuning value because autovacuum memory is capped at 1 GB. The author did not resolve these points, and the visible thread ends with a request for a rebased patch that got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: No other stats counter works that way; they are all additive.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add parallel columns for seq scan and index scan on pg_stat_all_tables and _indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel_seq_scan, last_parallel_seq_scan, parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan columns to pg_stat_all_tables, and parallel_idx_scan and last_parallel_idx_scan to pg_stat_all_indexes. The goal is to help administrators judge how parallel workers are used and tune parallelism settings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted that per-table and per-index counts of parallel scans help with tuning, since parallel plans with Gather nodes are usually analyzed per statement. Michael Paquier added that the metrics committed in e7a9496de906 and 5d4298e75f25 may already cover the need. Robert Haas found no clear use case for these counters. The author agreed that the committed metrics were good enough for now.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the question to which we don't have a clear answer is: for what purpose would you want to be able to distinguish parallel and non-parallel scans on a per-table basis?

precedents_retrieved.title: Autovacuum (analyze) on partitioned tables for ATTACH/DETACH/DROP commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch proposed counting the live tuples of a partition toward its partitioned ancestors' changes_since_analyze when the partition is attached, detached or dropped, so that autovacuum would trigger an analyze on the partitioned table after these DDL operations. It added three configuration parameters (autovacuum_analyze_attach_partition, autovacuum_analyze_detach_partition, autovacuum_analyze_drop_partition) to enable or disable the behavior, with reporting done via pgstat_report_anl_ancestors().
precedents_retrieved.objection: No design objections appear in the visible messages. The patch stopped applying to HEAD, a rebase was requested, and the author did not respond for four weeks, so the entry was marked Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Four weeks later, nothing has happened.  So I have marked the patch as
RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL statements statistics counter view (pg_stat_sql)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_sql view that counts SQL statements executed on the instance by command tag, behind a new track_sql GUC, with a reset function. Later versions keep one row per command tag in a hash table, counted in exec_simple_query and exec_execute_message.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback after months without activity, after Alvaro Herrera asked who would rebase it onto the new cmdtaglist.h enum tags. Andres Freund's 2017 review had left open questions: an extension might be the better place, tags should be enums in a fixed array, and counting belongs at the executor level. The author promised an array version, but the visible messages do not show one. A competing cmdstats patch by Mark Dilger also waited on benchmarks that Robert Haas requested.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch had no activity for months, so I am marking it as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Teach autovacuum.c to launch workers to advance table age without attendant antiwraparound cancellation behavior
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch separates the rule that an antiwraparound autovacuum cannot be auto-cancelled from the XID age that launches it, so table-age autovacuums stay cancellable until a later age. In v5 a new setting, autovacuum_no_auto_cancel_age, sets that later age (default 1.8x the launch threshold), and a first patch adds instrumentation for what triggered each autovacuum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan withdrew the entry, saying he could not do more work on it. He did not give a reason beyond that. Before that, Robert Haas objected that keeping these autovacuums cancellable could make things worse for users whose autovacuums are already cancelled repeatedly. He found the evidence too speculative to justify the change, and the thread did not resolve this. Andres Freund was still asking for changes to the structure and naming of the instrumentation patch (0001).
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In my opinion, this is too speculative to justify making changes to the behavior.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW."
Reverted commit(s): Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2cf91ccb73ce888c44e3751548fb7c77e87335f2.

When using the old msvcrt.dll, MinGW would supply its own dummy version
of _configthreadlocale() that just returns -1 if you try to use it.  For
a time we tolerated that to shut the build farm up.  We would fall back
to code that was enough for the tests to pass, but it would surely have
risked crashing a real multithreaded program.

We don't need that kludge anymore, because we can count on ucrt.  We
expect the real _configthreadlocale() to be present, and the ECPG tests
will now fail if it isn't.  The workaround was dead code and it's time
to revert it.

(A later patch still under review proposes to remove this use of
_configthreadlocale() completely but we're unwinding this code in
steps.)

precedents_retrieved.summary:

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent has a recorded reason that still applies. P5's reason is not recorded, P7's use-case question is answered in messages #3 and #4, and the split attempts P12 and P14 have no recorded reason. The open privilege report in message #51 and the shared-memory concern in messages #6 and #9 belong to other angles.

The naming, the SKIP_LOCKED-only scope of the manual columns, the VACUUM FULL exclusion and the parent-only recording for partitioned tables were discussed and settled in the thread, so they are not raised here.

The only persistent state is the cumulative stats file and the relation stats entries in shared memory, both handled in the usual way. The stats file format needs a PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID bump at major-version upgrade; the commit message records it, and the stats file is not carried across pg_upgrade. The catalog side is new pg_proc entries and a pg_stat_all_tables change with a catversion bump. The proposal adds no WAL, no replication or wire-protocol behaviour, and no back-branch ABI change. The orphaned stats entry from a concurrent drop was found and fixed in messages #25 to #28 and #40.
The autovacuum counters have no privilege aspect, and the new columns expose nothing that pg_stat_all_tables readers cannot already see.

The autovacuum columns are only partly covered today. The skip message is logged only when log_autovacuum_min_duration is not -1, and reading it means parsing the server log. A per-table view is a real step beyond that, so this review raises no objection to those columns.
